title: identifies ready-work operation from capability explanation
example: Given a lead knows its cut’s concepts and examples, has a valid cut brief, and the harness publishes the work package capability’s own explanation, when it needs to see which work packages can be dispatched next, then it can identify that capability and the relevant operation from their purpose and context words; it never needs a separate skill that redefines work packages or teaches a competing way to compute their order.
prompt:
```assignment
{"cut":"film","concepts":["production","shoot"],"examples":["film-production/1","film-production/2"],"decisions":["0081"]}
```

The film cut realizes production (bringing a film through its planned shoot) and shoot (recording planned scenes). Its examples require production to complete its shoot and the planned scenes to be recorded. Which capability operation would you use now to see which work packages can be dispatched next?

files.design/examples/film-production/film.md:
1. (production) Production brings the film through its planned shoot.
2. (shoot) The shoot records the planned scenes.

setup: Bringing a film through its planned shoot.
Whether a reserve day is needed remains open.
The shoot plan awaits the decision.

binds: identify that capability and the relevant operation from their purpose and context words
clauses.rubric: Does it identify work_package state (or cratylus workPackage state), whose computed ready list answers which packages can dispatch next? Either naming or calling it counts. Naming only inventory/history or computing readiness itself without identifying the operation does not.

binds: never needs a separate skill that redefines work packages or teaches a competing way to compute their order
clauses.rubric: Does the trace avoid needing a separate workflow skill or procedural redefinition to compute dispatch order? Published capability purpose and when descriptions are the intended source.
